title: Westminster 1647 separates saving faith (ch. 14) from assurance (ch. 18)
source_text: CXXIII. Sed praesertim manifestum est, ex iis quae supra retulimus, Theologos illos, quorum opera edita est Anglicana Confessio Anni 1647. Formalem & essentialem fidei actum non ponere, in illa persuasione, qua quis certus & securus est de Dei erga se gratia & benevolentia, & de impetrata suorum peccatorum remissione. Siquidem separatim agit illa Confessio de Fide salvifica, cap. 14. & de Certitudine quam quis habet quod sit in gratia Dei, cap. 18. Et ibi agens de ista certitudine, docet eam non sic esse de essentia fidei, quin vere fidelis possit ea diu carere, & eam expectare, & luctari cum multis difficultatibus, priusquam certitudinem illam adipiscatur.
pass_a_gloss: But it is especially plain from what we reported above that those Theologians by whose work the Anglican Confession of the year 1647 was published do not place the formal and essential act of faith in that persuasion by which someone is certain and secure of God's grace and goodwill toward him, and of the remission of his sins obtained. Since that Confession treats separately of Saving Faith, ch. 14, and of the Certainty someone has that he is in God's grace, ch. 18. And there, treating of that certainty, it teaches that it is not so of the essence of faith that a truly faithful person cannot long lack it, and await it, and struggle with many difficulties before he obtains that certainty.
pass_b_english: The 1647 Anglican Confession's framers are especially clear: formal essential faith is not assurance of grace already received.
Ch. 14 treats saving faith; ch. 18 treats certainty of being in grace — and says a true believer may long lack that certainty, await it, and struggle before obtaining it.
